memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'But houses in villages without walls around them are to be considered as
belonging to the open country. They can be redeemed, and they are to be
returned in the Jubilee. The Levites always have the right to redeem their
houses in the Levitical towns, which they possess'" - Lev 25:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God extends the redemption protections to village houses in the open
country, and He makes a special provision for the Levites. The Levites had
no farmland of their own; their inheritance was to serve God and live among
the tribes. So God ensured their houses were always redeemable, protecting
those who had chosen a life of service over accumulation.

Notice God's care for a specific group who were, by design, without the
usual security of land ownership. The very people who gave themselves to
serving the sanctuary were given particular protection.

Dear reader, God has always kept a special watch over those who lack the
ordinary safety nets. The Levite, the widow, the orphan, the foreigner —
these appear again and again as objects of His particular concern.

This should shape how we think about those in vocational ministry and
sacrificial service today. Paul taught that those who preach the gospel
should receive their living from it (1 Cor 9:14), and that elders who serve
well are worthy of honour and support (1 Tim 5:17-18).

More broadly, it should make us alert to anyone in our circle who has
traded security for service — the missionary, the carer, the volunteer.
God notices them. Do we?

Ask God to show you someone who has given up ordinary security to serve,
and consider how you might support them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who in my circle has traded security for service?
2. How could I support those in sacrificial ministry?
3. Do I share God's special concern for the vulnerable?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for Your care over those who give up security to serve
You. Make me generous and attentive toward them, reflecting Your own heart.
Amen.
